nodes.text: This is Hana Vesela. Requesting border passage through sector road B. Authorization code D-442.

answers.reply: I am transporting medical supplies to a house beyond the ridge. They are expecting me before morning.
Antibiotics. Bandages. Fever medication. Nothing illegal.

nodes.text: The road near the valley checkpoint was closed, so I had to take the longer route.

answers.text: Ask who is waiting for the medicine
answers.reply: A family outside the registered zone. The child has an infection.

answers.text: Ask if she has official delivery papers
answers.reply: The authorization should already be attached to my code.
Then please make your decision.

nodes.text: You can inspect the case if protocol requires it.

answers.text: Ask why medicine is needed outside the zone
answers.reply: Because not everyone inside the border receives treatment anymore.

answers.text: Ask if she knows the family personally
answers.reply: I know enough to understand they will not survive another night without help.
Then please make your decision.

nodes.text: The father used to work maintenance at the western transmitter station.

answers.text: Ask if they are registered citizens
answers.reply: Not anymore.
Because they asked questions at the wrong time.
Operator, please. I have already lost too much time.

nodes.text: You should see a temporary clearance attached to code D-442.

answers.reply: Because permanent approvals became difficult after the protests.
Central medical office. At least officially.
You have my code. You have the clearance.

nodes.text: There are entire settlements the system pretends no longer exist.

answers.reply: People talk quietly. Especially the sick ones.
You know enough now. Please decide.

nodes.text: I treated the girl once before. She could barely breathe.

answers.text: Ask why they cannot visit a state clinic
answers.reply: State clinics ask for identity verification first.
She needs the medicine. That is all that matters now.

nodes.text: Their records disappeared after the factory demonstrations.

answers.reply: I support keeping people alive.
I gave you the truth. Now decide what to do with it.

nodes.text: People who ask questions tend to disappear from forms very quickly.

answers.reply: Constantly.
I should not have said this much.

nodes.text: Hospitals treated injured workers. The administration did not like that.

answers.reply: I saw enough blood to stop believing official reports.
My clearance is valid. Please decide.

nodes.text: Most offices approve anything if the right stamp appears on the page.

answers.text: Ask if the documents are forged
answers.reply: I did not say that.
You have enough information.

nodes.text: I was not the first person they asked for help. I am only the first who came.

answers.reply: Let me pass, or stop me here.

nodes.text: If the system says you do not exist, the system does not treat you.

answers.reply: That is why I am here.

nodes.text: If that is a crime now, then write it down.

answers.reply: I am ready for your answer.

nodes.text: But fear is not a reason to let a child die.

answers.reply: Please make your decision.

nodes.text: They called it a minor disturbance. We ran out of bandages before midnight.

answers.reply: I will not justify myself further.

nodes.text: I said the code is valid. That is what your system cares about, is it not?

answers.reply: Check the code and decide.

nodes.text: Operator, I have given you my code and my reason. The child will not last the night without those supplies.

answers.reply: Thank you. I will proceed through route B.
Then I will turn back.
